text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me all right?
B: Yeah, I can hear you. Hi.
A: Hi. I'm Neil. Basingstoke.
B: Kerry. Bridgwater.
A: Oh right. Down past Taunton, isn't it? I've driven past it on the M5 on the way to Cornwall.
B: Everyone's driven past it. Nobody stops.
A: Ha. Fair enough.
B: So what do you do? I had you down as some sort of office boss, to be honest. Manager or something.
A: Er, not really. I'm a civil engineer, for the water company. I look after the pumping stations and the sewer networks round north Hampshire. So it's a fair bit of office, but a fair bit of standing in a field looking at a manhole as well.
B: Sewers. Right.
A: Somebody's got to. It's not glamorous, but when it goes wrong everyone notices.
B: That's the same with mine, to be honest. I'm a painter and decorator. Nobody looks at a ceiling unless you've done it wrong.
A: Yeah, that's true actually. Self-employed?
B: Yeah, just me. Domestic mostly, bit of work for a lettings agent. I've been up a ladder on a stairwell all day, so if I go quiet I've fallen asleep.
A: No, that's fine. I'm not much of a talker myself, so we'll sort of muddle along.
B: Ha. Okay. Do you have to go out in the night, then? If something floods?
A: Sometimes, yeah. I had one go at two in the morning a couple of months back. Pump station near the canal. You get the call, you put your boots on, you go and look at it. There's not much point getting worked up, you just sort of work through it. Then I came home and walked the dog, because she was up anyway.
B: What dog you got?
A: Labrador. Bramble. She's seven. I took her out just before this, actually, otherwise she'd have been whining at the door the whole time.
B: I've got a Staffie. Roxy. She's old now, she's got to have her teeth done at the vet's and it's going to cost me a fortune.
A: They're not cheap, are they. Bramble had a lump taken off last year. Karen, my wife, she nearly fainted at the bill.
B: Yeah, see, that's what I mean. Everything's gone up. Paint's gone up again this month. I can't put my prices up every five minutes, people just go and get some bloke off Facebook who does it for half and leaves a mess.
A: Yeah. We get that with contractors sometimes. Cheapest quote, and then you're paying twice to put it right.
B: Exactly. Then they ring me. Do you know what I mean?
A: Yeah, I do. Er, you got kids?
B: One. Jayden, fourteen. Football mad. I'm stood on a touchline every Sunday.
A: I used to play a bit. Five-a-side. Gave it up after I did my calf. Now I just watch Reading lose.
B: Did they lose?
A: They did. Again. Saturday. I've sort of made my peace with it.
B: Ha! I don't get why you'd keep watching, then.
A: My dad took me when I was a boy. You just do, don't you. That's about it really.
B: Fair enough. Are yours still at home?
A: No, both left. Daughter's in Southampton, she's a physio. Son's finishing at Nottingham. House is a bit quiet now. We've still got his room as it was, Karen won't touch it.
B: Oh, I'll be like that. I'll be crying in his room, won't I. Don't tell him I said that.
A: I won't. Er, I don't think I'll be meeting him.
B: No, you was never going to, to be fair.
A: Probably best. So what's—
